claims.statement: `getSharedConnection()` in `src/config/connection.ts` lazily creates and caches the app's single `@solana/web3.js` `Connection` from `env.rpcUrl`; if `EXPO_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` is unset it throws a setup-guidance error naming `.env.example`, so the failure surfaces at first chain access rather than at boot or module load.

`src/config/env.ts` maps three external-facing variables: `EXPO_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` → `env.rpcUrl` (used by both `getSharedConnection` and `fetchTokenFromRpc`), `EXPO_PUBLIC_HELIUS_API_KEY` → `env.heliusApiKey` (surfaced but not referenced by any code path — reserved for enhanced data fetching), and `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_MOCK=1` → `env.devMock` (forced on for all web runs).

Token metadata and per-token USD pricing are fetched by POSTing a Helius-style DAS `getAsset` JSON-RPC request (params `{ id: mint, displayOptions: { showFungible: true } }`) to `env.rpcUrl` itself — so the configured RPC endpoint must support `getAsset`; the key alone in `EXPO_PUBLIC_HELIUS_API_KEY` is inert.

`fetchTokenFromRpc` throws on both HTTP failures and JSON-RPC `error` payloads (no silent nulls); it maps `result.token_info` into the `TokenInfo` shape including `price_info.price_per_token`, the live-spot price that all value and PnL math is required to use.

`getCurrentSolUsdPrice` derives the SOL→USD price by fetching token info for `WRAPPED_SOL_MINT` (`So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`) through the cached `TokenService`, returning a validated finite number or `null` on any failure (logged, never thrown); `usePositionsPage` calls it on wallet change and refresh to feed the SOL/USD display toggle.

The production code's only use of the Meteora DLMM SDK is `DLMM.getAllLbPairPositionsByUser(connection, wallet)` in `PositionPipeline.loadPortfolio`, which returns a Map of pair address → `PositionInfo`; the call requires the Buffer polyfill installed by `index.js` importing `./polyfill` before the router, because the SDK's Anchor/buffer-layout deserialization needs Node Buffer methods Hermes lacks — SDK failures on Buffer methods are fixed in `polyfill.js`, not by forking the SDK.

`src/services/dlmmApi.ts` is the app-owned, typed transport for the officially documented Meteora DLMM Data API at `DLMM_API_BASE = 'https://dlmm.datapi.meteora.ag'`, replacing the `metcomet` dependency so wire types, error semantics, and pagination live in this repo; it serves `/positions/{pool}/pnl` (pipeline) and `/portfolio/open` (Android portfolio widget).

All DLMM Data API transport failures raise the typed `DlmmApiError` — carrying the HTTP status for non-OK responses and `status: null` for network-level rejections — with no silent nulls; the error explicitly marks pagination overrun, and callers catch and decide how to degrade.

List endpoints paginate at `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 50` driven by the server's `hasNext` flag, capped at `MAX_PAGES = 10`; `fetchPages` throws `DlmmApiError` if the cap is reached before completion rather than returning partial data, so `fetchAllPositionPnL` (pipeline) and `fetchOpenPortfolioSummary` (widget) are all-or-nothing — and because only resolved promises reach the cache, a mid-pagination failure leaves no cache entry and the next load retries cleanly.

USD and SOL money figures on the DLMM Data API wire (`usd`, `sol`, `pnlSol`, `balancesSol`, `totalDeposit`, …) are decimal strings that the transport never converts — consumers do. The only tolerated variance is `pnlSol`/`pnlSolPctChange`, typed `string | number | null` because older responses used numbers or omitted the SOL fields; legacy shapes normalize at the view-model boundary, not in the client.

`fetchOpenPortfolioSummary` walks every `/portfolio/open` page and surfaces the server-aggregated `total` (kept global across pages, as is `totalCount`), then rolls up the two fields the server does not: `outOfRangeCount` (Σ `positionsOutOfRange.length`) and a pool-value-weighted `feesTvl24h` (`parseFeePerTvl24h` converts the API's percentage string to an internal ratio; weighted by each pool's `balancesSol`, null when no weight).

`fetchOpenPortfolioSummary` deliberately does not roll up per-pool `totalDepositSol`: that figure is gross and double-counts redeposits after a withdrawal (documented in the client docstring), so the widget derives its deposited figure as `totalValueSol - totalPnlSol` from the server's own value/uPnL pair instead (ADR 0002).

`fetchPoolOhlcv` fetches display-only candles from `GET /pools/{address}/ohlcv?timeframe=…` on the DLMM API base (duplicated as local constant `METEORA_DLMM_API`); it is a pure fetch with no caching or singleton, supports timeframes `5m|30m|1h|2h|4h|12h` with default `'4h'`, coerces string-valued fields to numbers, tolerates a missing `data` array as empty candles, and throws on non-OK responses.

The OHLCV series is denominated in the pool's native Token X / Token Y ratio — the same units as a bin's `pricePerToken` — which lets `PriceChart` share one axis between the candle line and a position's Range low/high prices with no conversion; the data is display-only by ADR 0001 and must never feed PnL or value computation, and `usePoolOhlcv` serves a deterministic mock series in `env.devMock`.

ADR 0001 (`docs/adr/0001-no-local-historical-pricing.md`) is binding across all integrations: every monetary value derives from live-spot prices (`TokenInfo.price_info.price_per_token`, SOL via the wrapped-SOL mint); there is no local historical price computation (no OHLCV for math, no Pyth benchmarks, no local historical-SOL lookup) — historical-SOL PnL comes from the server's aggregated endpoints; and OHLCV is the sanctioned display-only carve-out.

ADR 0001 records that local historical pricing was built and removed twice (a `PriceService` with OHLCV + Pyth fetchers, deleted as fully orphaned; a Helius-based true-SOL-numeraire PnL, rejected in the Pass 2 audit), each time duplicating server work and risking a second PnL definition disagreeing with Meteora's displayed numbers — so future 'value-over-time chart' or 'local real-SOL PnL' proposals start from this decision rather than re-deriving it.

`createDataServices()` (`src/services/data.ts`) wraps the raw RPC and OHLCV fetches in `CacheManager` and exposes `TokenService` (`getPrice`/batch `getPrices`, cached 60 s under `token_data:{mint}`) and `OhlcvService` (`getOhlcv`, cached 60 s under `ohlcv:{pairAddress}:{timeframe}`); the batch fetch runs per-mint under `Promise.allSettled` and omits mints whose fetch rejected, so partial RPC failure returns the successes and the pipeline tolerates missing entries as `null` token info.

The Android portfolio-summary widget's data path (`syncPortfolioWidget` → `updatePortfolioWidget.fetchPortfolioSummary` → `fetchOpenPortfolioSummary`) uses only the DLMM Data API client — no RPC connection, no SDK, no Helius key — so it works whenever the API is reachable, and it fails hard on `DlmmApiError` by rendering the widget's error state.

External-surface dependencies are injectable for tests: `PositionPipeline` accepts `PipelineDeps` (`cache`, `connection`, `dataServices`), `createDataServices` accepts a fresh `CacheManager`, and pipeline tests run the real `dlmmApi` client with its real pagination against a stubbed `globalThis.fetch` while mocking only the SDK and token fetchers.
